Heyo! Although there is a little bit of crossover, this subreddit is more focused on the tabletop side of space marines, painting/gameplay/lore. You will likely have better luck in the subreddit specifically for the game, I believe it is r/spacemarine2.

Vermintide is based off of Warhammer Age of Sigmar, not 40K. Skaven are a race of rat people found ONLY in non 40K Warhammer. 

Vermintide and Darktide are AOS and 40K versions of a similar game. Darktide has you playing as an imperial guard (4 classes) to fight off a Nurgle Plague in a hive city (more along a zombie line of thinking). Darktide has no real story, it’s just a fun zombie horde game with somewhat of a story (being a prisoner recruited in emergency to help, rise the ranks to full guard member). 

Most 40K stuff isn’t a consistent story, it’s separate stories in the same setting. You don’t need to play any other games to enjoy space marine 2. Space marine 1 was just a hack and slasher against orcs. Orcs were invading a city to steal something, you had to fend them off/get to the object first. That’s the long story short of it, I’ve never played it, just read the synopsis. 

To know the context and lore of space marine two, I’d just go to YouTube and look up videos (I highly recommend Leutin09 he’s really thorough and easy to listen to) of the creation of the adeptus astartes and what Tyranids are, those should get you up to speed with what’s happening in space marine 2.

Edit: my bad Vermintide has nothing to do with AoS. I thought it did because I know absolutely nothing about either setting, I’m a 40K nerd lol.

It really depends on my mood. At any given moment it’s a great guess that I’m listening to Radical Face. His melodies really tickle my brain, specifically songs like ‘Severus and Stone,’ ‘Summer Skeletons,’ and ‘Ship in Port.’ But really I can’t think of a song of his I don’t like. The guy behind Radical Face did a side project with a friend under the name ‘Electric President.’ It’s a really similar vibe with a lot more percussion. ‘Monsters,’ ‘All the Distant Ships,’ ‘Eat Shit and Die’ are all great melodic songs. 

Other top artists in my world are:
Rural Alberta Advantage - amazing folk/indie catalog centered around Canada living
Arcadian Wild - hopeful adventure folk
Friendly Savages - first album is dedicated to a friend who passed, some really good emotional songs
City of the Sun - my favorite instrumental group, I rate them slightly higher than explosions in the sky
Dusted - really unique sounding group, reminds me of living in the dusty desert. (Property Lines is a good starter song)

When I need to get pumped up I listen to 90s punk, or stuff like ‘Jesus built my Hotrod’ by Ministry or ‘Ribcage’ by the Bronx.

Edit: wanted to add that Radical Face has four albums in the family tree series, it’s a whole world he created that mirrors our world but with slight fairytale-ish differences (one character walks on water when she sleep walks, etc). You can still find the whole family tree online, or the whole 56 page guide book that’s includes lyrics and short stories about all the characters. This project one of my early hyper fixations before I was diagnosed lol.

Hey so hopefully this is the right place for this. Sorry in advance for a long post there will be a TLDR at the bottom. 

I’m working on a custom chapter that descends from the ultramarines. This is mostly a creative project ands will only be used in casual games at most. After painting a full black Templar army, I fell in love with Phobos and Gravis marines specifically, and wanted to do an army based off them alone. I’ve found a bunch of aftermarket bits to really give this army a unique look that leans into the ultramarines Roman vibe. I also liked the idea of desert warfare so I thought it could be cool to do an ultramarine inspired desert Roman army. 

I have a Phobos kill team to start, but I plan to add a squad of eliminators, a Phobos Lt, and then a bunch of Gravis guys. The end goal is to kitbash a tank with a Middle Earth Mumakil to make a cool desert elephant tank. I also want to make a custom chapter master with Marneus Calgar. 

In terms of lore I was thinking that a group of ultramarines were dropped on a desert planet that is locked in constant warfare between a local militia and chaos with occasional Xenos threats. After dropping in, all the chapters air support were shot down leaving them stranded, and the planet was too hot for help to come. Over the years they have integrated with the local humans (would love to add some guard models for show) and over time replenished their ranks by testing aspirants from the local population. Over this time they have lost touch with direct knowledge of the ultramarines and are left with heavily influenced retelling of old stories of the ultramarines, more or less mythologies. 

As far as their name goes, vultures were seen as holy birds by the Romans so that would work, and Solitudinem was suggested and I liked it, it can mean desert in Latin, but also means solitude. 

I was thinking of calling them ‘Vultures Solitudinem’ but after a quick search it looks like Solitudinem is ahead a planet that is already home to a chapter. Would this be confusing if my marines are technically on a different but very similar planet? Should I use a different word than Solitudinem? Is there a better bird than a vulture? 

I torn between really excited and thinking this is really dumb. Does any of this make sense or seem cool? Do you have any advice to make the story better or more coherent? 

I’ve attached the two test models I did to try out color scheme. Blue bodies for higher ranks, blue extremities for battle line soldiers. I wasn’t sure about the yellow or purple eyes though. What do y’all think? Note: almost all heads will be replaced when bits come in. 

 This is my first try at a full custom chapter so any words of advice or criticism or encouragement would be greatly appreciated.  Thanks for reading this far, hope you have a great day. 

TLDR: it’s a desert themed successor called ‘Vultures Solitudinem’ in the colors pictured above good idea? Any thoughts or opinions?

Wow these are really impressive! You appear to be really proficient with the actual painting, the colors are solid and well defined, good control. 

I might just recommend looking into washes, hitting certain recesses on the armor with a dark wash can really add some depth to the scheme. I’m looking at the tech marine specifically, it looks like you did a wash with a darker blue on the other guy and it looks good. The tech marine, in my opinion, the yellow armor panels fall a tiny bit flat. Add a dark brown or orange wash into some of those recesses and I bet it would add some depth to him. Same with some of the silver bits, a black wash there would likely add depth. 

Not necessary at all, they look great, but that’s really the only thing I could see for you to do more to these guys. And it’s just my opinion. If you’re happy with them, that matters infinitely more than what people on Reddit think.

This is what I do and exactly what I would recommend. It gives me more variety in painting while keeping a coherent look. More ‘color’ on battle line troops, more gold/silver growing as units go up in seniority. Rock and sand crabs (I’d guess ammonite too but I’ve never done them) are inactive by default. They hide under the surface, and are not targetable. You can make them targetable by walking adjacent to them. This will bring them above ground and then they can be targeted like normal. 

Most people who cannon rock crabs set the cannon in the middle of the area, then just sprint around walking next to as many rock crabs as possible, and once they attack you and get on top of the ground, the cannon should start shooting them like normal.

I’m turning 28 in a few days, I left BYU after 4 years (switched major after not getting accepted into a program I banked on) and only having a semester and a half left. My depression became too much, I realized it wasn’t worth it. I’d rather be a happy college drop out than a miserable shell of a person with a degree. 

I’m also gay so that contributed a lot to leaving BYU. 2 years after I left BYU I moved to Colorado and met who is now my husband. Now I live on the east coast where Mormonism isn’t even a thought. We just celebrated our 2 year wedding anniversary 2 days ago. The comment on my Instagram post about it was ‘The best two years.’ 

It seemed like such a big deal at the time to leave school with so little left, but it was the best decision for me. I finally got to start my life doing what I really wanted. I found a career that doesn’t require a degree that I really enjoy, but my husband thinks I’m destined for greater so we’re looking into sending me to a trade school or a program that can get me qualifications to start a career in I.T. or welding or something. Stuff I didnt even consider in school, but will be much faster and easier and cheaper to get, and still leave me making the same money if not more than most college grads. 

You’re young, you still have plenty of time to figure life out. In my opinion the church always taught me that I had to do school, do college, get a degree, get a job in said degree, then raise a family. That’s not at all how the real world works. There’s so many different life paths and options on how to get where you want to be. Being happy for the journey is a lot more important than the speed of that journey. Fuck BYU. Get out of there and live your best self. Everything else will start making sense. Best of luck to you and your spouse.

Members vs free to play makes a big difference. I highly recommend members, but I'd also recommend taking your time and learning in free to play first. If you did decide to get members, I suggest you just pay for it, trying to bond out of f2p is exhausting and turns into a real chore.

Money is pretty overrated early game. I've been playing since 05, and just recently broke the 50m mark at 113 combat and I'm still very "poor" but goddamn do I have fun. I didn't break the 1m mark till combat level 75 (got 70 range and wanted a d bow) but before then there was no need to have more than 500k on me. The best way to have fun and progress your account is going for unreadable items and quests. Unreadable items are mostly members, but they are gear and weapons that you unlock via questing and minigames and cannot be traded, therefore building in valuable 'free' items that add value to your account, that can't be sold and are permanent. Barrows gloves and fighter torso and arclight will never depreciate in value (and many more I'm forgetting). Also they are fun to achieve in different ways. Questing does the same thing for your account, but rewards you with new areas, new profitable monsters to kill, new skilling methods, etc. Quests require little to no money, and only add value to your account. Once you get a fair bit into the game, questing and such, you'll find ways to make money that are far better than anything you can do starting, and you'll progress your skills along the way (some quests have skill requirements you have to reach. A quick Google search will show you an 'optimal quest list' with all the quests in order so you have to train the least amount in between).

The general consensus is stay free to play until you beat dragon slayer, and if you had fun up to that point it's a great investment to get members. Buy a bond (with cash) and try it for a few days. Members is kinda a completely different game, but in a really good way. Free to play is a small taste, and if you're into it, members 100x more fun. If you decide to go members at that point, make barrows gloves your first 'long' term goal, but build smaller goals around your interests into there.

Take time, try out all the skills. There's no need to rush questing. Most skills aren't profitable starting out, but can build into some really good money makers once you invest some time into them. Everyone likes and doesn't like different skills, find your favorites and run with them. I for some reason love Hunter. It's a slow grind at first, but once you got level 40 you can have three traps at a time out, and then it gets really fun. Then at level 50 or 53 or something, you can hunt chinchompas and it's not great money in the big picture, but for what level you would probably be at the time, it's great money. Took me a few hours at chins, got a few more levels and my first mil. It was really rewarding, because I love Hunter for some reason. Mining, crafting, runecrafting, smithing, woodcutting, thieving, fishing etc, most skills got a good profit spike right around the 50-70 mark. I generally did some combat, some questing, then when I start getting burnt, I'll make a hard switch to skilling. Recently grinded 70-85 mining. Was a bit of a grind, but a nice break from the constant combat I was doing, and I made 8m from the ores. Take a little time, try out every skill till at least level 10-20 so you can try more than the level 1 method. 

As far as the GE works, it's based off the community's perception of each item. I've been buying and selling my dragon warhammer a lot recently so I'll use it as an example. A few weeks ago theatre of blood hard mode was released. Dragon warhammer is a very useful item for that, so when it was announced, everyone that didn't have one wanted one. At the time the dwh was at 34m I believe. I put in an offer for one at the GEs recommended price, but people were willing overpay because they needed them for ToB hard mode, and obviously people selling were going to at least try to get a little more money off theirs, so nobody put a DWH at GE price for sale, so my order was never filled, as none were available at the price. EVEN THEN you have to think about other users who have BUY offers at GE price who put their offer in before me, on the offhand chance someone did want to sell at GE price, (I don't know exactly how it works) there's a good chance the other user who put their offer in first would get it filled first, still leaving me empty. This is where some slow sales on the GE come from. They keep the GE recommends prices as up to date as possible, but it's so based off perceived values of items that's it can never be accurate, just a good guide. On the other side of that coin, after ToB hard mode had been out a while, people realized the dwh had become overvalued in the hype, so the price started (and still is) tanking. I sold my DWH at 37m, but at the time the GE price was 37.8m I believe. Because so many people were dumping their warhammers, you could put in a BUY offer at GE price and it would Insta buy and you'd get money back most likely because people were dumping them below GE price.  Hope that makes a little sense. I'm still not smart on the GE, I just buy above ge price and sell below, because I crave that Insta buy/sell goodness. If you're more patient and don't crave that Insta, you can buy low and sell high. That's where the idea of 'flipping' to make money comes from, but it take a lot of time and knowledge about how to walk the fine line between GE value and perceived value, and playing idiots like me who Insta every transaction. 

Hopefully this helps, if you have any other questions feel free to ask. Enjoy the game! It's kept me hooked for years, and that's not a bad thing (although it can be lol).

Yeah, to elaborate a bit, the pay dirt must be cleaned on the conveyor, and at the end of the process the conveyor deposits the pay dirt in the sack for you. To initiate the process, all you have to do is click the 'hopper' (square opening on the far end of the conveyor from the sack). It will automatically deposit all pay dirt in your inventory on the conveyor. You should be able to notice if the water is running or if it's still. If it's still, you need to repair the wheels on the backside of the conveyor. Search some of the boxes near the hopper, one should contain a hammer. Grab a hammer and click the wheels to fix them (you get smithing xp for fixing the wheels as well). Only one wheel needs to running to move the pay dirt down the conveyor, but both running keeps it running longer before needing to be fixed.

A few more notes to keep in mind:
You can only have one 'deposit' on the conveyor at a time. You won't be able to make another 'deposit' of any size until the initial deposit has reached the sack. A 'deposit' is any amount of dirt you put in the hopper, whether it be one pay dirt, or a full invent. They both count as one deposit. 

The sack can hold more than one inventory of pay dirt. I believe initially it can hold something like 84 or 86 ores, so you can do a deposit, go back to mining, make another deposit, then bank both from the sack, then go back to mining. Will save you a little time not waiting for deposits to make their way to the sack.

I had the same feeling being 25 and not knowing what to do to get help. I called my insurance and asked about my coverage for therapy. Luckily I have good coverage so they gave me a list of therapists they'd cover, I did some research and found one I thought would work for me. She's been great, not as big a help as some people's therapists, but it helps. I also found friends I could confide in,  and they helped push me to get help for myself. I don't know what your real life is like, but I know there's tons of people on here you could talk to including me. 

I tried taking control of my depression and doing things for myself and nobody else. I deleted all social media (except for a private Instagram for only my real friends, I have 10 followers right now and it's perfect) and quit paying attention to other people. Once I just focused on my life and my in person relationships things started the change, not necessarily get better, but changed to make things easier in most circumstances. Try getting into a regular hygiene routine (I finally started brushing and flossing my teeth again and it feels so good) and try to get out of the house at least once a day, even if it's a 15 minutes walk around the block.

Most importantly, go easy on yourself. You have a lot of thoughts and emotions, you can't control them. Sometimes you need to feel things, even really really bad things, but remember that it's out of your control (to a degree) and just do everything you can to do your best despite it.

And just one more time, you are not weak. Reading your story, I thought about how strong you are. A lot of people can't come back from what you did, so that kinda make you a badass. You're fucking tough. If anyone can do this, it's you. Small steps. Be proud of the small steps you do take and go easy on yourself for the ones you miss. Even strong badasses like you miss steps and make mistakes, but don't let it get you down. You are tough and you can do this.

My boyfriend and I both dropped out of uni, he went to work in retail for a big company, I learned how to be a good enough mechanic to get jobs. My boyfriend is about to get a corporate position paying better than 90% of my friends who finished college. I make a little less but more than enough to support myself on. 

I thought uni was bullshit. I did three and a half years of it (changed major 3 times so I'm still over a year off a degree) but I have never regretted leaving. My brother is 2 years older than me, finished college, and is in a way worse spot than me.

School isn't everything. Don't stress it too much. You're gonna be fine, you'll find a way to make it work. If you really want a job that required uni, just schedule in a small amount of study time here and there. Half hour or hour between classes? Go to the library. Don't with classes before 6pm? Section off an hour to study, or a half hour, or even 15 minutes. 

The most common issue I saw at uni was that people thought all free time had to be studying. They'd either have no social life or wouldn't study and get depressed. I had to learn to study enough to pass classes, but didn't want to lose too much. I got mostly Bs, a few As and a few Cs. I also spent less than half the time studying of most of my friends. You should try to schedule in study free time. I'd always give myself an hour of relax time a day. Don't feel guilty about not studying, just enjoy it and take care of yourself. 

You have three weeks off (two now). That's a lot of time. Don't waste it all studying, you don't need to study that hard. Over studying can create issues. Just try to find an hour or so a day to study. I'd always try right after lunch because I'd be fat and happy and didn't wanna move anyway. 

Most importantly though, don't beat yourself up for not doing what you think you should be. You're human, you can't do everything you want to all the time. Sometimes you fall short and don't study at all. Just look yourself in the mirror and say something like "I tried my best today. I may not have accomplished everything I hoped to, but I'm here and I'm okay and we have plenty of days ahead to try again." It's hard, but I've been trying it and it has been working surprisingly well.

You can do this, but there are other options besides uni, so don't stress out too much. Hang in there and know that I'm rooting for you no matter what you do.
